title: Fitting ML-UMR Models
text: mlumr() function fits Bayesian multilevel unanchored meta-regression models using Stan. default backend rstan; cmdstanr can used installed configured. Three outcome families supported: binary (binomial), continuous (normal), count (Poisson). Two model types available family: SPFA (Shared Prognostic Factor Assumption): shared regression coefficients across treatments Relaxed SPFA: treatment-specific regression coefficients, allowing effect modification

title: Fitting ML-UMR Models
text: SPFA model assumes covariates affect outcomes equally treatments. model : logit(P(Yi=1|Index))=μA+𝐱iT𝛃 \text{logit}(P(Y_i = 1 | \text{Index})) = \mu_A + \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta} logit(P(Yj=1|Comparator))=μB+𝐱jT𝛃 \text{logit}(P(Y_j = 1 | \text{Comparator})) = \mu_B + \mathbf{x}_j^T \boldsymbol{\beta} 𝛃\boldsymbol{\beta} shared across treatments. AgD likelihood integrates comparator population covariate distribution using QMC points. Relaxed model allows treatment-specific effects: logit(P(Yi=1|Index))=μA+𝐱iT𝛃A \text{logit}(P(Y_i = 1 | \text{Index})) = \mu_A + \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}_A logit(P(Yj=1|Comparator))=μB+𝐱jT𝛃B \text{logit}(P(Y_j = 1 | \text{Comparator})) = \mu_B + \mathbf{x}_j^T \boldsymbol{\beta}_B captures effect modification covariate effects differ treatments. difference 𝛅=𝛃A−𝛃B\boldsymbol{\delta} = \boldsymbol{\beta}_A - \boldsymbol{\beta}_B quantifies treatment--covariate interaction.

title: Fitting ML-UMR Models
text: continuous outcomes, SPFA model : Yi|Index∼Normal(μA+𝐱iT𝛃,σ2) Y_i | \text{Index} \sim \text{Normal}(\mu_A + \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}, \sigma^2) AgD likelihood uses mean standard error observed outcome. generated quantities include mean differences (delta_index, delta_comparator) primary treatment effect measure. additional prior_sigma parameter controls prior residual standard deviation σ\sigma. default half-normal prior induced Stan’s <lower=0> constraint; half-Student-t exponential priors also available prior constructors.

title: Fitting ML-UMR Models
text: count outcomes exposure, SPFA model uses Poisson likelihood log link: Yi|Index∼Poisson(exp⁡(μA+𝐱iT𝛃)⋅Ei) Y_i | \text{Index} \sim \text{Poisson}(\exp(\mu_A + \mathbf{x}_i^T \boldsymbol{\beta}) \cdot E_i) EiE_i exposure (person-time). AgD likelihood uses log-sum-exp numerical stability. generated quantities include rate ratios (delta_index, delta_comparator).

code: library(mlumr) set.seed(2026)  # --- IPD for Drug A --- n_A <- 500 age_A <- rbinom(n_A, 1, 0.40) sex_A <- rbinom(n_A, 1, 0.55)  # True model: logit(p) = -0.5 + 0.8*age - 0.3*sex logit_p_A <- -0.5 + 0.8 * age_A - 0.3 * sex_A y_A <- rbinom(n_A, 1, plogis(logit_p_A))  ipd_df <- data.frame(   trt = "Drug_A",   outcome = y_A,   age_group = age_A,   sex = sex_A )  # --- AgD for Drug B --- # True comparator model: logit(p) = -0.8 + 0.8*age - 0.3*sex # (same covariate effects, different intercept) n_B <- 400 age_B <- rbinom(n_B, 1, 0.35) sex_B <- rbinom(n_B, 1, 0.50) logit_p_B <- -0.8 + 0.8 * age_B - 0.3 * sex_B y_B <- rbinom(n_B, 1, plogis(logit_p_B))  agd_df <- data.frame(   trt = "Drug_B",   n_total = n_B,   n_events = sum(y_B),   age_group_mean = mean(age_B),   sex_mean = mean(sex_B) )

code: library(mlumr) set.seed(2026)  # --- Prepare IPD (index treatment) --- n_A <- 500 ipd_df <- data.frame(   trt = "Drug_A",   outcome = rbinom(n_A, 1, 0.55),   age_group = rbinom(n_A, 1, 0.40),   sex = rbinom(n_A, 1, 0.55) )  ipd <- set_ipd(ipd_df, treatment = "trt", outcome = "outcome",                      covariates = c("age_group", "sex"))  # --- Prepare AgD (comparator) --- agd_df <- data.frame(   trt = "Drug_B", n_total = 400, n_events = 148,   age_group_mean = 0.35, sex_mean = 0.50 )  agd <- set_agd(agd_df, treatment = "trt",                      outcome_n = "n_total", outcome_r = "n_events",                      cov_means = c("age_group_mean", "sex_mean"),                      cov_types = c("binary", "binary"))  # --- Combine and add integration points --- dat <- combine_data(ipd, agd) dat <- add_integration(dat, n_int = 64,   age_group = distr(qbern, prob = age_group_mean),   sex = distr(qbern, prob = sex_mean) )  # --- Run all three methods --- # Naive (instant) naive_result <- naive(dat)  # STC (instant) stc_result <- stc(dat)  # ML-UMR SPFA (Bayesian, takes a few minutes) fit <- mlumr(dat, model = "spfa",              prior_intercept = prior_normal(0, 10),              prior_beta = prior_normal(0, 2.5),              chains = 4, iter = 4000, warmup = 2000, seed = 42)  summary(fit) marginal_effects(fit, effect = "lor")
